newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus could keep less than 51 pct of Telepiu.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus could keep less than 51 pct of Telepiu.

text.p: French pay-television group Canal Plus could reduce its stake in Italian broadcaster Telepiu to less than 51 percent, Canal chairman Pierre Lescure told Le Monde in an interview.
Canal Plus increased doubled its stake in Telepiu to 90 percent last week after a deal with Germany's Leo Kirch.

"It is clear that STET and RAI will have a significant stake. But Mediaset and Canal Plus also want to see, with smaller stakes, a number of other Italian industrialists," Lescure was quoted as saying.
"Canal Plus will not necessarily have a 51 percent stake. Some could even see that as a symbolic provocation. We do claim management and operational control," he said.

Lescure said in the interview that Canalsatellite, a digital satellite television service in France, now had more than 400,000 subscribers and would be "largely" above the 500,000 at the end of the year.

He said that Canal Plus would launch a 24-hour news channel in the spring of 1998 at the latest. "The project is actively pursued. There are still one or two decisions to take. Not on the creation of the channel but on the format and the editorial line," he said.
